text: Social procurement is the practice of leveraging inclusive economic opportunities from institutions purchasing and capital investment activities. For example, an institution can make efforts to purchase goods and services from suppliers from underrepresented communities and social enterprises. An institution can also embed employment and training requirements in large capital projects. Social procurement is part of the City of Toronto's own purchasing procedures. In 2017, the first year of implementation for social procurement, the City awarded more than $550,000 in City procurement contracts to diverse suppliers, and included employment and training requirements in 17 large-scale City infrastructure projects. City Council on March 26 and 27, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the Executive Director, Social Development, Finance and Administration to enter into an agreement with the Atkinson Foundation to deliver a third phase of AnchorTO and to receive $115,641 in grant funding from the Atkinson Foundation to deliver the initiative. 2. City Council increase the Approved 2018 Operating Budget for Social Development, Finance and Administration by $56,309 gross, $0 net, and include the funding for the second year of $59,332 gross, $0 net in the 2019 Operating Budget Submission for Social Development, Finance and Administration, with the possible extension of the AnchorTO Program to be included in the 2020 Outlook, if required to complete the delivery of the Program.
